raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Supersedes #61760 (open since 2026-10-15, not tested on the DSpark draft). Credit for the idea and the kernel changes goes to the author of #61760.



## Purpose

Make the Triton unified-attention split-K (3D) launch usable for a **non-causal sliding-window** multi-query decode, and make it split the **window** instead of the whole sequence.

This is #61760 (zhentaocc) rebased on current main and narrowed to what we could validate; the idea and the kernel changes are theirs (`Co-authored-by` on both commits). What is different from #61760:
- Rebased on current main, and only the two kernel changes (below) plus tests. No new heuristics.
- Measured on gfx950 (MI355X) with a real model: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash DSpark draft (window 4096, 5 draft layers, 16 q heads : 1 kv head per rank at TP4, head size 128, fp8 KV and fp8 query, block size 128, 7 query rows per request).
- Tests for that shape (below) and a negative control: with the pre-change kernel/helper, 137 of the 270 `splitk`/admission tests fail.

### Why it matters

DSpark/DFlash drafters run **non-causal** attention: `config/speculative.py` does `dflash_config.setdefault("causal", False)`, and the MiniMax-M3.1 draft is all sliding-window (4096). On main:
1. non-causal multi-row decode is excluded from split-K (`or not use_causal`), so the draft always takes the **2D launch**, one program per query row, each walking the whole window serially (~129 tiles of 32 keys, ~1.4 us/tile);
2. even where split-K is used, `tiles_per_segment` is computed from the full `seq_len`, so at long context the window falls in one or two of the 16 segments and the others return immediately.

In-server profile (rank 0, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP4, 150K-token requests, 5 draft layers): `kernel_unified_attention` is **179 us per call, 0.89 ms per decode step**, independent of batch and context, with no `reduce_segments` kernel (the 2D path), i.e. ~8-10% of the decode step.

### Changes
1. `compute_tile_loop_bounds`: with a pruned sliding window, split the window's tiles over the segments (`reduce_segments` is unchanged; its segment count still derives from `seq_len`). Shared by the diff-KV kernel, whose reducer uses the same formula.
2. `unified_attention`: admit non-causal rows (`max_seqlen_q <= MAX_3D_QUERY_LEN`) to split-K, with at least `min(next_power_of_2(num_seqs), 8)` tiles per segment for non-causal launches (kernel and `reduce_segments` get the same constexpr).

Scope: validated end to end only on the MiniMax-M3.1 DSpark draft (non-causal, window 4096). Other non-causal users (other DFlash drafters, other backends) and other window sizes are covered by the unit tests only.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k "splitk or admission"
```
New tests (all compare against the existing reference, extended with a non-causal window mask):
- `test_splitk_segments_split_sliding_window`: segment bounds tile the window exactly, causal and non-causal, windows 64/1024/4096, seq_len 40..150000, min-tiles 1/2/8.
- `test_splitk_sliding_window_long_context_matches_reference`: windows 64/1024, causal and non-causal.
- `test_splitk_draft_sliding_window_shape_matches_reference`: 16q:1kv, head 128, window 4096, 7 and 8 rows, 1-24 requests, context 1K-150K, block size 16/128, bf16 and fp8 Q/KV, causal and non-causal; asserts the split-K launch.
- admission test: non-causal multi-row now takes split-K.

## Test result (MI355X, gfx950)

- Unit tests, this branch: **2350 passed, 3 skipped** (`test_triton_unified_attention.py` + `_diffkv.py`); the `splitk or admission` subset is 270 passed. Negative control (same tests on the pre-change helper and ops): 137 failed.

### Kernel (one rank's shape, HIP graph of 5 calls on 5 distinct caches; us per call; max abs diff vs an fp32 reference 1.3e-3..2.0e-3 for both)

| N requests (ctx 150K) | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 118 | 119 | 119 | 119 |
| this PR | 14.6 | 20 | 31 | 47 |

| context (N=1) | 1K | 2.5K | 4.1K | 5K - 500K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 32 | 74 | 118 | 118 |
| this PR | 8 | 10 | 14 | 14 |

In the server, per call (profiler, 60-iteration windows): N=1 179 us -> 19.6 us (+ `reduce_segments` 4.6 us); N=8 178 us -> 40.9 us (+ 4.9 us). Per decode step (5 layers): 0.895 ms -> 0.121 ms (N=1), 0.891 -> 0.229 ms (N=8). (Isolated-kernel absolute times are lower than in-server because the isolated benchmark runs on hot caches; the ratios are what to compare.)

### End to end (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, DSpark 7 draft tokens with synthetic acceptance length 4.04, 150K-token prompts, decode chunk-gap p50, ms; median of 3 runs, range in parentheses)

Against unmodified attention/MoE files (the other local patches reverted), plus the same comparison on top of our patched install (same installed state both sides):

| N | 1 | 2 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 10.35 (10.34-10.36) | 10.87 (10.81-10.90) | 12.67 (12.58-12.84) | 14.39 (14.35-14.43) | 14.63 (14.60-14.83) | 16.22 (16.12-16.35) | 17.79 (17.74-18.26) | 19.55 (19.47-19.58) |
| this PR | 9.52 (9.51-9.55) | 10.16 (10.10-10.17) | 11.96 (11.84-12.02) | 13.61 (13.59-13.96) | 13.93 (13.78-13.99) | 15.44 (15.43-15.49) | 16.99 (16.96-17.16) | 18.98 (18.96-19.00) |
| change | -0.83 ms (-8.0%) | -0.71 (-6.5%) | -0.71 (-5.6%) | -0.78 (-5.4%) | -0.70 (-4.8%) | -0.78 (-4.8%) | -0.80 (-4.5%) | -0.57 (-2.9%) |

On the patched install (N=1,2,4,5,6,8; 3 runs): main 9.33 / 10.22 / 11.84 / 12.90 / 13.27 / 14.58 -> PR 8.55 / 9.33 / 10.99 / 12.09 / 12.60 / 14.06 (-8.4% / -8.7% / -7.2% / -6.3% / -5.0% / -3.7%).

### Accuracy

Real (non-synthetic, `rejection_sample_method=standard`, greedy) acceptance length, chat requests at 2K/8K/30K/100K context, 6 requests per length, same prompts: main 3.90 (5368 accepted / 1852 drafts) vs this PR 3.92 (5378 / 1839). Greedy outputs are not bit-reproducible run to run on main either (first divergence 13-400 characters between two runs of the same prompt on main, the same range as main-vs-PR), so equivalence is judged by acceptance length.

Not included (follow-up): the split-K admission threshold `128 // num_heads_kv` leaves 19-32 concurrent requests on the 2D launch (7 rows each). Raising it to 256 (same scratch size when `max_num_seqs <= 64`) measured -2.1% / +0.5% / -0.9% / -2.4% / -1.2% decode step at N=12/16/20/24/32 (8K context, max-num-seqs 64), below the noise-plus-benefit bar, so it is left out.

 from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_unified_attention import (
     MAX_3D_QUERY_LEN,
+    NON_CAUSAL_MAX_MIN_TILES_PER_SEGMENT,
     reduce_segments,
     unified_attention,
 )
@@ -117,7 +118,7 @@ def launch(grid):

         (5, {"causal": "per_sequence"}, False),

@@ -393,6 +394,7 @@ def ref_paged_attn(

 ) -> torch.Tensor:
     num_seqs = len(query_lens)

@@ -677,6 +687,7 @@ def test_triton_unified_attn(

+        causal=causal,

@@ -783,6 +796,7 @@ def test_triton_unified_attn(

+        causal=causal,
     )
     atol, rtol = 1.5e-2, 1e-2
     if q_dtype is not None:
@@ -1251,3 +1265,138 @@ def test_softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores() -> None:
     ref = soft_cap * torch.tanh(scores / soft_cap)
     assert torch.isfinite(out).all(), out
     torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sliding_window", [64, 1024])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("causal", [True, False])
+def test_splitk_sliding_window_long_context_matches_reference(
+    monkeypatch, sliding_window, causal
+):
+    """Split-K over a window much shorter than the sequence."""
+    reduce_grids = _spy_reduce_segments(monkeypatch)
+    test_triton_unified_attn(
+        seq_lens=[(8, 8), (8, 1100), (8, 4097), (1, 3000)],
+        num_heads=(8, 2),
+        head_size=128,
+        sliding_window=sliding_window,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        block_size=16,
+        soft_cap=None,
+        num_blocks=1024,
+        q_dtype=None,
+        seq_threshold_3D=32,
+        causal=causal,
+    )
+    assert len(reduce_grids) == 1
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _compute_window_segment_bounds(
+    output_ptr,
+    seq_len,
+    context_len,
+    USE_CAUSAL: tl.constexpr,
+    SLIDING_WINDOW: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_SEGMENTS: tl.constexpr,
+    MIN_TILES_PER_SEGMENT: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    TILE_SIZE: tl.constexpr = 32
+    segm_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    tiles_per_segment = tl.maximum(
+        tl.cdiv(seq_len, NUM_SEGMENTS * TILE_SIZE), MIN_TILES_PER_SEGMENT
+    )
+    loop_lo, loop_hi, _ = compute_tile_loop_bounds(
+        context_len,
+        seq_len,
+        seq_len - context_len,  # cur_batch_query_len
+        0,  # q_block_local_idx
+        segm_idx,
+        tiles_per_segment,
+        TILE_SIZE,
+        16,  # BLOCK_M
+        8,  # BLOCK_Q
+        2,  # num_queries_per_kv
+        SLIDING_WINDOW,
+        False,  # USE_MM_PREFIX
+        True,  # IS_3D
+        USE_CAUSAL,
+    )
+    tl.store(output_ptr + 2 * segm_idx, loop_lo)
+    tl.store(output_ptr + 2 * segm_idx + 1, loop_hi)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("min_tiles", [1, 2, NON_CAUSAL_MAX_MIN_TILES_PER_SEGMENT])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("causal", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_len", [40, 600, 4096, 4103, 32768, 150000])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("window", [64, 1024, 4096])
+def test_splitk_segments_split_sliding_window(
+    causal: bool, seq_len: int, window: int, min_tiles: int
+) -> None:
+    """3D segments tile the pruned window exactly (no gap, no overlap), using
+    only the segments that reduce_segments reads."""
+    num_segments, tile_size, query_len = 16, 32, 8
+    bounds = torch.empty(2 * num_segments, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+    _compute_window_segment_bounds[(num_segments,)](
+        bounds,
+        seq_len,
+        seq_len - query_len,
+        USE_CAUSAL=causal,
+        SLIDING_WINDOW=window,
+        NUM_SEGMENTS=num_segments,
+        MIN_TILES_PER_SEGMENT=min_tiles,
+    )
+    bounds = bounds.view(num_segments, 2).tolist()
+
+    tiles_per_segment = max(triton.cdiv(seq_len, num_segments * tile_size), min_tiles)
+    read_segments = triton.cdiv(seq_len, tiles_per_segment * tile_size)
+    first_key = max(seq_len - query_len - window + 1, 0)
+    last_key = seq_len - 1  # the non-causal right window ends at seq_len too
+    want = list(range(first_key // tile_size, last_key // tile_size + 1))
+    got = [t for lo, hi in bounds[:read_segments] for t in range(lo, hi)]
+    assert got == want
+    # The window is spread over the segments, not walked by one or two.
+    longest = max(hi - lo for lo, hi in bounds[:read_segments])
+    assert longest <= triton.cdiv(len(want), read_segments)
+
+
+# The shape one TP4 rank runs for the MiniMax-M3.1 DSpark draft: 16 query heads
+# sharing 1 KV head, head size 128, non-causal sliding window 4096 (dspark sets
+# dflash_config.causal=False), a block of 7 (8) draft query rows per request.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("num_reqs", "context"),
+    [
+        (1, 1024),
+        (1, 4103),
+        (1, 30000),
+        (1, 150000),
+        (3, 150000),
+        (8, 30000),
+        (24, 5000),
+        (24, 30000),
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("query_len", [7, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [16, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("q_dtype", QDTYPES, ids=["bf16", "fp8"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("causal", [False, True], ids=["noncausal", "causal"])
+def test_splitk_draft_sliding_window_shape_matches_reference(
+    monkeypatch, num_reqs, context, query_len, block_size, q_dtype, causal
+):
+    reduce_grids = _spy_reduce_segments(monkeypatch)
+    # Distinct, uneven lengths so segments see different window offsets.
